title: Roasted Long Hots and Red Peppers
description: Italian long hots and sweet red peppers charred until smoky, peeled, and dressed with olive oil, garlic, and salt.

items: ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing

steps.title: Heat the broiler
steps.text: Set an oven rack 4 to 6 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Line a baking sheet with foil.

steps.title: Char the peppers
steps.text: Lay the long hots and red bell peppers on the sheet whole and brush the long hots with a little olive oil. Broil, turning every few minutes, until blistered and blackened all over: about 8 to 10 minutes for the long hots and 15 to 20 minutes for the red peppers. Take each out as it finishes.
steps.why: The char gives the smoky flavor and loosens the skins. Long hots have thin walls, so they finish well before the thick red peppers.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Put all the charred peppers in a bowl while they’re still hot and cover it tightly for 15 minutes.
steps.why: Trapped steam lifts the blistered skins so they slip off.

steps.title: Peel and seed
steps.text: Peel the red bell peppers, pull out the stems and seeds, and tear them into wide strips. Rub the loose skin off the long hots and leave them whole. A few flecks of char are fine.
steps.why: Wear gloves for the long hots. Their heat varies from pepper to pepper, and it stays on your fingers.

steps.title: Dress and rest
steps.text: Layer the long hots and red peppers in a dish with the garlic and salt, and pour the olive oil over the top. Let them sit for at least 30 minutes before serving.
steps.why: Resting lets the garlic and salt season the oil, and the peppers soak it up.

notes.Serving: Serve at room temperature with crusty bread, on an antipasto platter, or on a sandwich.
notes.Storing: Cover and refrigerate. Because the garlic sits in oil, eat them within 4 days. Let them come to room temperature before serving.
